title: Dragon
snippet: The Ancient Dragon residing in the Dragon Shrine is said by the Emerald Herald to have watched over the world for "aeons". However, the veracity of this is doubtful, and he may have been resurrected by Lord Aldia instead of being a survivor from the War of Fire, since Aldia attempted to recreate the dragons using giant souls. The former is far more likely as when the Ancient Dragon is slain, the Bearer of the Curse receives a Giant Soul. He gifts the Ashen Mist Heart, a manifestation of ashen mist whose magic can allow one to delve into the memories of the long-deceased, such as dead Giants and even a Dragon, as well as to pull items and souls from those memories into the real world. Whether this is an actual magic of the Dragons that the Ancient Dragon's body manages to inherit is unknown, but it remains doubtful since the Ancient Dragon may be a false Dragon.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - prologue 
 prologue : The Bearer of the Curse became undead at some point, hollowing until they had no recollection of their former life. Desperate to find a cure, they were drawn to the walled off kingdom of Drangleic, where a cure to the undead curse was rumored to exist. Journeying through a portal and guided by a Fire Keeper, the Bearer of the Curse found themselves in the Things Betwixt. Finding there a hut with the remaining Fire Keepers, the Bearer of the Curse is made to remember more of their past and is cured of their hollowing through a Human Effigy. The Bearer is then guided towards Majula to seek the Emerald Herald.

The Herald, in turn, tells the Bearer of the Curse to seek the king, Vendrick, to find their answers and claim the throne, but warns that the Bearer will never find the king with a soul so pallid, instructing them to seek out the four Great Ones and to claim their power.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: Through another questline, the player can cooperate with Yuria, a leader of the Sable Church of Londor, who urges the Ashen One to take the Flame for themselves, to usher in an Age of Dark; for the Sisters of the Sable Church were under the guidance of Kaathe. This is Ending 4: "The Usurpation of Fire", where the Flame is wrested by the Ashen One, who is to lead the Age of Man as the Lord of Hollows. By the time of *Dark Souls III*, the undead curse has been accepted by the people of Londor, who have come to view it as a blessing, and their Hollow form as the "true face of man".

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
The Bearer of the Curse will journey through the Black Gulch to find the fallen kingdom of Shulva, Sanctum City, once ruled by the Sunken King. The king ruled the city, centred around the worship of a slumbering dragon known as Sinh, until his kingdom was invaded by the Drakeblood Knights lead by Sir Yorgh, who sought to claim the dragon's blood. Sir Yorgh slew the king, and awoke the dragon, which proceeded to kill him and lay waste to the city with its poison. The Bearer of the Curse slays Elana, the Squalid Queen, a child of the Abyss, and the dragon Sinh to claim the Sunken King's crown.

Next, the Bearer of the Curse returns to the Old Iron Kingdom, to seek the Old Iron King's crown. Finding the kingdom under the sway of another child of the Abyss, Nadalia, Bride of Ash, the Bearer braves their way through the ruined towers to find the Fume Knight, who guards the crown of the Old Iron King.

title: Vendrick
snippet:
Vendrick -  Dark Souls II - boss - plot 
 plot : After an untold amount of time in confinement, the King of Drangleic remains a hollowed husk of his former self. The player may choose to spare the king, leaving him to wander eternally, or slay him and end his misery.

Using the Ashen Mist Heart, the Bearer of the Curse may also enter the Memory of the King, where they may interact with King Vendrick as he was before he went hollow. Bitter and grieving his failures, Vendrick tells the Bearer to seek the crowns of old kings of yore. Once they have brought him all the crowns, Vendrick will unlock their power, making the Bearer of the Curse immune to the hollowing effects of the curse. He advises the Bearer of the Curse to seek a third path beyond Light and Dark, echoing his brother.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Finally, the Bearer of the Curse travels to Frozen Eleum Loyce, once ruled by the Ivory King. Built to contain the Old Chaos, the city was abandoned and froze over when its king vanished into the chaos. Guided by the last child of the Abyss, Alsanna, Silent Oracle, the Bearer of the Curse seeks out the remaining knights of Eleum Loyce to gain their help in braving the Old Chaos. Finding the Burnt Ivory King there, the Bearer of the Curse defeats him and claims his crown.

Once the Bearer of the Curse has found all three crowns of old, along with Vendrick's own crown, the fallen king will unleash the hidden power of the crowns, making the Bearer of the Curse immune to the hollowing effects of the curse. Bidding the Bearer to seek strength, and asking them whether allowing the flames to fade is truly their only choice, the king sends the Bearer of the Curse on their way.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet: When about to light the last primal bonfire, the Bearer of the Curse is surprised by the Scholar of the First Sin, who emerges from the bonfire. The Scholar asks if they want to "shed the curse", unless they have already joined the crestfallen, he tells them that there are two paths: to inherit the order of the world, or destroy it. He admits that very few have come this far, and yet the Bearer's journey is far from over. The Scholar asks of the Bearer to seek Vendrick, "he who almost became a true monarch", for he will guide their way. After this, the Scholar will disappear, letting the Bearer of the Curse light the primal bonfire.

title: Bearer of the Curse

 four_great_ones : The Bearer of the Curse sets out to find the Four Great Ones.

Through the rotunda in Majula, the Bearer of the Curse makes their way to the ancient domain of the Old Iron King, whose hubris led to his death beneath the molten iron, where he was possessed by the soul of one whose name must not be repeated. Making their way through the king's old hunting grounds and the now poison-filled valley surrounding the castle, the Bearer of the Curse finds and slays the Old Iron King, claiming his soul for their own.

By way of ship or on the wings of an eagle, the Bearer of the Curse makes their way to The Lost Bastille, a forgotten prison where the Lost Sinner is held. The Lost Sinner was imprisoned for the sin of attempting to relight the First Flame. The Bearer of the Curse fights their way down into the very bottom of the prison, where they face the Sinner and take her soul for their own.

title: Nashandra
snippet: Left without a king and with no means to claim the Throne of Want, Nashandra’s plans were stalled until the arrival of the Bearer of the Curse, an undead powerful enough to defeat the Four Old Ones and gain access to Drangleic Castle. Nashandra manipulated the Bearer of the Curse into opening the way to the Throne of Want by aiding them in seizing the Throne of Want. She directs the Bearer of the Curse toward the Undead Crypt, suggesting that they put an end to the now-hollowed King Vendrick and claim his ring. She then directs the Bearer of the Curse to journey to Aldia's Keep to acquire the Ashen Mist Heart, and warns them that the Ancient Dragon there is no more than a prop and a false deity. At last, she directs the Bearer of the Curse toward the Forest of Fallen Giants to visit the memories of the Giants and obtain the last key to the Throne: the Giant's Kinship.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet:
Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin -  Dark Souls II - boss - strategy 
 strategy : Aldia is immobile when fought, but is able to teleport, releasing an area of effect attack around the area he teleports to.

Several of Aldia's attacks deal mixed Fire and Dark damage, so some form of fire defense is recommended for this fight. All of his attacks deal either pure physical or Fire/Dark damage. This means that a shield that is highly resistant to both physical and Fire/Dark damage, such as the Rebel's Greatshield, will reduce his damage output greatly.

The Fire Orbs have moderate tracking, so rolling may be needed to fully evade. Forbidden Sun can be cast in any direction, even directly behind him. The Fire Orb and Forbidden Sun attacks can be avoided by rolling, strafing around Aldia or running perpendicular to their trajectory.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet: The deformed Aldia is encountered several times by the Bearer of the Curse, to whom he imparts his extensive knowledge on the nature of life. He expresses outrage over the actions of the Lord of Light, who cursed humans into mortality and introduced the cycle of light and dark by linking the First Flame. Aldia's bleak worldview considers mankind as "props on the stage of life", persevering merely through obsession. While acknowledging the merits of the Age of Fire, he labels the roots of this "warm, resplendent" world as a lie, with the linking of the Fire as its original sin. Nevertheless, Aldia realizes that one could wish to inherit this order, even if built on a "tender, exquisite" lie. Instead of submission to the peace provided by the status quo, he offers a third "path"; obscure and unpaved, yet could perhaps ascend the scope of Light and Dark.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet:
Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : Aldia is the elder brother of King Vendrick, and aided his brother in founding the kingdom of Drangleic. He secluded himself in his manor, searching for secrets of life, viewing the Undead as the key to finding it. For his reverence of the Undead, Aldia was shunned by Vendrick, banished to his Keep forever. People who were invited to his manor commonly disappeared and were replaced with malformed beasts. The Southern and Northern Ritual Bands were created by Aldia and his acolytes after cruel, horrible experiments were performed on these people. Many valuable objects came out of Aldia's Keep, including the Sunset Staff, the Spitfire Spear, Soul Geyser, Unleash Magic, and Forbidden Sun.

Through his experiments, Aldia sought to learn the nature of the undead curse, and to shed the yoke of fate. He failed, however, and turned into a monstrosity, inhabiting the bonfires.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin

If the conditions are met, he can serve as the final boss of *Dark Souls II*, with his fight triggering after Nashandra's; he, notably, is the only boss in any *Dark Souls* game not to die when defeated, and as such drops no souls nor items, with the player instead gaining the option of an alternate ending in which the Bearer of the Curse is hinted to as following this mysterious other path at Aldia's side. He is also a mentioned character in *Dark Souls III* via the Soul Stream description, which refers to him as "**the first of the Scholars**". snippet:
The withered tree branches he utilizes inflict physical damage only, making them especially prone to being blocked. At a distance, the branches extend out of the ground in a path in front of him, with moderate tracking, making it harder to roll out of the path of the attack. This aura also bolsters his own defenses, reducing the damage he receives from all attacks by a significant amount. The fiery aura fades when he performs certain moves, giving the player a small window to attack up close. The first opening is just after he teleports to a new location, and the second is when he is charging up his Forbidden Sun attack.

title: Ancient Dragon
snippet:
Ancient Dragon -  Dark Souls II - boss - strategy 
 strategy : Going hand in hand with its size, the Ancient Dragon has a huge amount of health and will most likely kill the player in one shot with every attack unless the player has high Fire defense or a very high stability shield. Its most dangerous and most common attack is when it flies up and breathes fire on to the floor, covering a large area.

The startup for this attack is obvious, however, so once one sees the attack coming, they can run away. When it lands, the forward fire breath can be baited out by standing somewhere in front of it. This allows the player to run behind the dragon's head and land a few hits.

Another strategy is staying near its tail, it gives a constant direction to run to and most of the flame attacks won't reach the player when they are at the end of it. It does, however, have a tail slam that inflicts a lot of damage, but it's easily avoided.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
At the bottom of the gaping hole in Majula lurks things long forgotten. Here, The Rotten, a hideous amalgamation of corpses awaits. After making their way through The Gutter, a place where unwanted things have been discarded, the Bearer of the Curse faces down the Rotten itself in its lair, slaying it and claiming its soul for their own.

After freeing Rosabeth of Melfia from her petrification, the path is now open from Majula to Brightstone Cove Tseldora. The Brightstone Cove Tseldora once housed a prosperous town, grown rich after its founder, the Duke Tseldora, discovered its massive crystal deposits. The Duke was always a peculiar figure however, obsessed with spiders, and one day, a massive spider known as The Duke's Dear Freja and her countless children overran the town, and the Duke was never seen again. Fighting their way to the spider's lair, the Bearer of the Curse slays the beast and finds the final Great Soul hidden in her lair.

title: First sin
snippet: Similarly, after the Lords were successful in defeating the Ancient Dragons, Gwyn used his Soul to build a civilization above-ground, for humans to worship the gods in; allowing the Furtive Pygmy's descendants to come out of their abyssal caverns and live in the sunlight. The gods built a city of castles above this world from which to rule, and effectively made ingress impossible without great strength. However, in the stead of humanity taking the plunge into sin, it is Anor Londo, following the lead of its king. Thus - perhaps symbolic of this inversion - humankind becomes damned to eternal life instead of the persistent death of reality; and the gods of *Dark Souls* become ineffectual rulers, where systems similarly devolve into chaos in real life, but as designated by Providence.

title: First sin
snippet: The term "First Sin" is likely derived from the Judeo-Christian account of humankind's [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Original_sin original sin], generally agreed amongst most sects to be a base flaw in all people stemming from the original humans, Adam and Eve, partaking in the fruits of a certain tree in the Garden of Eden; the sole action God strictly forbade that they do under threat of death. This fruit opened their eyes, allowing them to see and "be as God, knowing good and evil", but in disobeying God they effectively caused humans to be branded by Him as untrustworthy and capable of sin. He then cast them out of the Garden and had them toil for their food all their lives. Most significantly, however, was that there was a second tree within the Garden that bestowed everlasting life, with God Himself saying "and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever" before casting the pair out to eventually die.

A life that, like the humans', was not bound by the death. title: Marvelous Chester
snippet:
**Unlike Kirk, who can only invade three times in the entire game, Marvellous Chester will invade indefinitely unless his human form is killed.
Chester bears a close resemblance to the [https://demonssouls.fandom.com/wiki/Fat_Official Fat Officials] from *Demon's Souls*, permanently grinning ministers of vile character, as well as some of the game's cut NPCs.
**He also shares a few similarities to characters and aesthetics found in *[https://bloodborne.fandom.com/wiki/Bloodborne Bloodborne]*, which notably began development around the time that work on the *Artorias of the Abyss DLC* was being completed. His dark, Victorian attire and eccentric personality would fit right in with the setting of [https://bloodborne.fandom.com/wiki/Yharnam Yharnam]. His quick sidestepping dodge is also slightly reminiscent of the way Hunters dodge in that game, as opposed to the dodge rolls more common in the *Dark Souls* series.

title: Marvelous Chester
snippet: Despite doing this, Chester will still sell items to the player, either mocking them for coming to him after the invasion if he killed them, or speaking in a rather disgruntled tone as if being mocked by the player coming back if he is the one who was defeated. To stop all invasions permanently, the player will need to kill him there, which is also the only way to receive his unique set. Of course, killing him before he ever even invades will also prevent him from doing so in the first place.

title: Marvelous Chester
snippet:
He was also seemingly more involved with Elizabeth at some point, as all his cut dialogue makes reference to her. He was supposed to have a fascination with her peculiar sorceries, as well as chastising the player for siding with her against him. This would all explain why the mushroom lady seems to consider him odious in the final game.

His unscrupulous nature appears to have been toned down significantly from his inception, even though he continues to be shady and tracherous all the same in the current version of the story.

title: Marvelous Chester
snippet:
Marvelous Chester -  Dark Souls - character - location 
 location : He is encountered in the Royal Wood, to the right of the coliseum where the fight with Knight Artorias takes place, past a short bridge. He leans against the cliff face, highlighted by a lit candelabra to his right. He remains there for the rest of the game.

He will invade as a red phantom early into Oolacile Township, on the descending walkway after the first Bloathead Sorcerer. This only happens if the player is human.

title: Marvelous Chester
snippet: Despite appearing relatively friendly, he will take the first chance he can to backstab the Chosen Undead, ambushing them in the town of Oolacile for an unclear reason. Should the hero find the betrayal unacceptable, they can challenge the real version of Chester and slay him for his transgression. However, inheriting his equipment, more specifically his peculiar grinning mask, will cause them to make the same expression underneath it. This is believed to be the result of his vengeful spirit itself; the curse of Chester.

title: Marvelous Chester
snippet:
Marvelous Chester -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Marvellous Chester is a mysterious man who, much like the Chosen Undead from the time of Lordran, was snatched by Manus and stranded in the past. He met with Oolacile Sanctuary's keeper, Elizabeth, making quite the negative impression before departing. He is later met by the time traveling hero, offering his wares should they need them.

His attire is of an exquisite quality, betraying an aristocratic origin, as well as lending itself extremely well to stealth. That fact, coupled with his ownership of a Sniper Crossbow, suggests that the man may be one of Carim's snipers from far into the future, though nothing is truly certain with someone as shrouded in mystery as he is.

title: Marvelous Chester
snippet:
He bears some resemblance to V, the main protagonist of the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V_for_Vendetta *V for Vendetta*] graphic novel. Both characters are incredibly agile in melee combat and they are known for using masks with a permanent grin to cover their faces. Also, Chester uses peculiar projectiles in the shape of roses, and the rose is one of the many symbols that are commonly associated with V.
His permanent grin could be in reference to the Cheshire Cat from *[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice%27s_Adventures_in_Wonderland Alice in Wonderland]*. If that's the case, his name could act as an allusion to this, as [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chester Chester] is the main town in the English county of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheshire Cheshire].

title: Marvelous Chester
snippet:
Marvelous Chester -  Dark Souls - character - strategy 
 strategy : For most unsuspecting players, Marvellous Chester will appear behind them as they descend whenever he invades, getting the chance of firing a few shots in their back. Being at long range, he is capable of firing multiple bolts at the player in quick succession, possibly dealing heavy consecutive damage.

However, being at mid-range is also quite dangerous, as his bolts alternate with a different kind of rose-shaped projectile, which can quickly rack up damage. These flowers in particular are very troublesome, as they greatly build up Bleed and he throws three of them in a horizontal arc, spreading out and giving them more of a chance to hit the player. He is not without his tricks at close range, performing sweeping low kicks that do a fair amount of damage and stamina drain.

title: Marvelous Chester
snippet:
Marvelous Chester -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : Marvellous Chester is found very close to Artorias' arena and sells a variety of useful items such as Green Blossoms, various moss clumps, some offensive consumables, and other utility items, albeit for a higher price than normal. This makes him a very convenient stop for stocking up on items for the nearby boss battle or for the Battle of Stoicism unlocked right after.

Unfortunately, he will invade the player whenever they get to Oolacile Township, provided they are human. Unprepared players may be taken by surprise, especially since he has a completely different moveset compared to the usual red phantom NPC. Vanquishing him once won't actually stop him from invading another time, as he will always return every time the area is reloaded.

title: Marvelous Chester
snippet:
Marvelous Chester -  Dark Souls - character - cut_content 
 cut_content : There's an alternative model of Marvellous Chester without his coat and iconic top hat. This variant wields a peculiar black and gold Zweihander, which has an unused weapon model that would have allowed players to wield it. What this version of Chester was going to be used for is unknown.

According to [https://youtu.be/ny5B9Hxn6KA?t=56 cut dialogue] from Lord's Blade Ciaran, a ring that belonged to Artorias would have been stolen by someone she describes as "a man in a long coat". The only character in the DLC that matches that description is Chester, implying he'd be more involved in the sidequests initially. The player would have to obtain the stolen ring from him, possibly by force.

title: Marvelous Chester
snippet: It's good to remember that Chester also has an unusually high amount of HP for an NPC, likely due to his more varied and unique moveset. He is also able to dodge attacks from the player and create distance between him and them by elegantly side-stepping away from them in a spinning motion, much differently from the dodge rolls of other NPCs.

He's voiced by William Houston, who also voices King Vendrick in *Dark Souls II*, [https://bloodborne.fandom.com/wiki/Retired_Hunter_Djura Retired Hunter Djura] in *[https://bloodborne.fandom.com/wiki/Bloodborne Bloodborne]*, and Oceiros, the Consumed King in *Dark Souls III*.

**The special Hornet Ring animation will not play when parrying/backstabbing Chester, nor can the Dark Hand be used to drain humanity from him like with every other human NPC.
**This may also be the reason why he is the only invader encountered in the game that does not leave a Bloodstain upon being defeated.
He is the only other invader besides Kirk, Knight of Thorns who can be defeated more than once per playthrough.
**Unlike Kirk, who can only invade three times in the entire game, Marvellous Chester will invade indefinitely unless his human form is killed.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Giant (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - enemy - variants 
 variants : Giants specialize in several different types of combat and can be differentiated by their appearance. Giants use their brute strength to great effect. Many of the soldiers who invaded Drangleic used large clubs, or even just their fists in battle. Some giants utilized a form of pyromancy, while others were known to have the ability to produce toxic projectiles from their bodies.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Giant (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - enemy - appearance 
 appearance : Their heads are largely absent of facial features, apart from a large gaping mouth-like hole at the center. Its function seems to be similar to a mouth, as indicated by the roars that are emanated from within, but Giants have also been known to extract balls of poison and fire from them. Their bodies are covered in a rough, rock-like skin. The upper half of their bodies is generally bulky, with huge protruding shoulders and massive arms, however some are more slender in appearance. They largely wear rudimentary clothing, such as loincloths and ragged robes.

Their brutish appearance and primitive weaponry has led some citizens of Drangleic to view them as being no more than uncivilized barbarians, but contrary evidence shows that they utilize magic and employ concepts such as monarchy and military hierarchy.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet:

 lead : **Giants** are a race of enormous humanoids from a land vaguely described as "across the seas" from Drangleic. They can vary in size, but generally they tower over most beings. Possessing colossal strength, their willpower is said to be as strong as steel and their souls are incredibly powerful.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet:

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Giant (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - enemy - war_with_drangleic 
 war_with_drangleic : Giants are primarily known through their conflict with King Vendrick and his kingdom. According to legend, a mysterious woman named Nashandra, said to be of unparalleled beauty, came to Vendrick long ago and warned him of a looming threat across the seas, in the land of the Giants. King Vendrick named Nashandra his queen and crossed the ocean with her to combat the Giants. During this conflict, he pillaged the Giant's lands, and stole an unspecified "prize", which he brought back to Drangleic. Using this acquired power, Vendrick created various types of Golems, who in turn built Drangleic Castle.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet: Battles waged endlessly between Vendrick's forces and the Giants, and much of Drangleic's citizens fled the kingdom to escape the conflict. Ultimately, the Giants were defeated by an unnamed hero. In the aftermath, much of Drangleic had been reduced to rubble, and visitors to the kingdom were rare. Many Giants were killed in the conflict, and their corpses eventually grew into large trees that sprawled across the once prosperous kingdom. The last known Giant to have survived the conflict was terribly wounded and kept prisoner in a cavern beneath the Forest of Fallen Giants. It was later discovered another two Giants survived the war, but remained hidden in a cavern in Black Gulch.

They wear a hooded robe and their left arm is coated in a green substance, which can poison anything it hits. This type of Giant can be encountered in the Memory of Vammar.

snippet:

 melee_giant : A more common, gray, shorter type of Giant that fights mainly with a large club or fists in battle. They can be encountered in the Memory of Vammar and Orro.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet: While the Giants invasion was largely stopped, their souls remained powerful. King Vendrick's elder brother, Lord Aldia, kept Giants in his manor and performed experiments on them in an attempt to recreate a dragon. The outcome of Lord Aldia's experiments is unknown, but oddly when the Ancient Dragon roosting at the summit of Aldia's realm was slain, the soul of a Giant was found in its remains. Legend holds that the Giants' resentment of King Vendrick was possibly emboldened in death. This was proven true when the Bearer of the Curse fought the hollowed remains of Vendrick. With the souls of several Giants in the Bearer's possession, Vendrick was significantly weakened and subsequently defeated.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet: Seeking vengeance for the subjugation of his kingdom, the king of the Giants amassed an army in a vengeful counter-invasion of Drangleic. He also sought to reclaim the invaluable "prize" stolen from him. Unwilling to forgive the actions of Vendrick, the Giants crossed the sea and landed on the northern shores of Drangleic. They set siege to Drangleic Castle and relentlessly attacked various settlements, forts and keeps across the land for several generations.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)

A plunging attack against the smaller Giant variants will trigger a sync attack that causes the player to stand on their shoulders for several seconds and then strike them directly in the face before stepping off. The Giants are weak to Dark and Magic.

**Gliding Stab: **Has a similar tell to the gliding slash: Sir Alonne will hop backwards then execute a stab attack. This attack drains a lot of stamina if blocked.

When the Iron King was at the peak of his rule, Sir Alonne left him to travel the lands for an unknown reason. For his service the Iron King bestowed Alonne's name to his knights.

title: Sir Alonne
snippet:
**Dark Sword**: Similar to Dark Greatsword. If the player is some distance from him, Sir Alonne will unleash several horizontal waves which cause magic damage upon impact.

**Impale: **Sir Alonne will charge up for a moment before lunging towards the player, impaling them with his sword if he connects. This is a grab attack and therefore cannot be blocked. The attack drains health from the player and buffs Alonne's sword for roughly 40 seconds.

**Parry and Riposte: **Similar to The Lost Sinner, Sir Alonne will sometimes change the way he holds his sword, almost appearing as though he is attempting to block. Should the player attempt to attack him in this pose, Sir Alonne is able to parry and then riposte the player, dealing a large amount of damage.

**Kick:** He will kick the player if they are constantly shielding oneself. High stamina drain.

title: Vendrick
snippet:
Vendrick -  Dark Souls II - boss - strategy 
 strategy : Vendrick has very high defenses, which can potentially make this a very lengthy fight. However, his defenses can be considerably lowered by collecting up to five Souls of a Giant found throughout Drangleic. Each Soul of a Giant halves his defense. Without any souls, he has 32 times his base defense and takes almost negligible damage per hit. Even with the Souls of a Giant, Vendrick is not to be taken lightly. His attacks deal heavy damage, have good reach, and can stagger players who roll too early because of the windup for each one.

 lead : **Vendrick** is an optional boss in *Dark Souls II* and a non-playable character in .

He is voiced by William Houston, who also voiced Marvelous Chester in *Dark Souls* and Oceiros in *Dark Souls III*.

title: Vendrick
snippet:
Vendrick holds his sword with the blade dragging behind him even as he winds up for the horizontal slash attacks. Staying close to him and strafing to his left will make it very hard for him to hit the player. He will sometimes jump back to put distance between him and the player. If he backs up into a wall, the player may back up in an attempt to get behind him again. Keeping a good shield ready can help, but not always, as most of Vendrick's attacks have extremely high stamina damage.

A good way to approach the fight is to stay directly behind or next to his left foot. If he gets too close to a wall where any part of the player or him is bumping into it, try to lure him back out toward the center of the arena.

title: Vendrick
snippet:
**Single Sword Swing**: Will swing the sword horizontally towards the player once, it has a long reach, and a slow wind-up that is exactly the same as the swiping. Fairly easy to dodge by sprinting towards his left side. He will also do this is the player is far away and will most likely kill them if their back is turned.

**Charge**: If the player starts really distancing themselves from Vendrick where he can not hit them with his swing, he will pick up speed. He will move much faster than his normal slow meander and will most likely catch the player off guard if they were healing or buffing their weapon. The best way to handle this is, if one has a shield, to raise it and sprint towards his left side. If one doesn't have a shield, sprint towards his left side and be prepared to roll for your life.

**Curse Orb**: Upon crossing the fog wall, Vendrick will scream and throw a dark red orb at the player, inflicting instant curse if it connects.

title: Vendrick
snippet:
Vendrick -  Dark Souls II - boss - drops 
 drops : Vendrick will not drop anything except the given amount of souls when he dies. However, his soul and his armor set can be found in the Shrine of Amana, behind a door that can only be opened after defeating him. The door is in the area between the first and second hut where the player can find a pathway leading to the door, however, they must be in human form to open it.

Using a Bonfire Ascetic instead of going to NG+ will not spawn these items anew in the Shrine of Amana.

title: Vendrick
snippet:
Vendrick -  Dark Souls II - boss - notes 
 notes : Vendrick is initially passive, and will aggro only upon taking enough damage from the player. This is affected by the number of Giant Souls in the player's possession, so attacking him in his initial encounter after the battle with Velstadt will not aggro him.
By using a Bonfire Ascetic at the Undead Ditch bonfire, Vendrick can be respawned, but so will Velstadt.
If Vendrick is killed before going and slaying Nashandra, the player will have to fight Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin, which can ultimately cause Aldia to be the third boss in a row, assuming the Throne Watcher and Defender are not yet defeated.
If a player summoned for the Velstadt fight has any Souls of a Giant in their possession they will reduce Vendrick's defense immediately after the fight. If the area is abandoned or the player dies in that first fight he will reset and only calculate the player's Giant Souls.

title: Vendrick
snippet:
Vendrick -  Dark Souls II - boss - attacks 
 attacks : **Swiping**: Swipes his sword across the ground two or three times in a row. This is his deadliest attack, as if it hits the player's shield it will drain all stamina and the player will then by severely damaged or killed by the following swing. Hugging **his** left foot while causes the attack to completely swing over the player's head, but rolling through the attacks works well too if the player learns Vendrick's moveset and timing.

**Overhead Sword Slam**: Raises his sword up and slams it onto the ground, sometimes done twice or even three times in a row. Easy to dodge by staying as close to him as possible.

**Jump Attack**: Will jump towards the player and slam his sword into the ground where they were standing the moment he jumped. There's a clear wind-up and it is fairly easy to dodge by moving out of the way when he gets airborne.

title: Spear of the Church
snippet: These holy warriors are all that stands between the Ashen One and the sleeping princess, who presumably held the key to obtaining the Dark Soul. Even the last of the Spears falls to them in time.

title: Ending (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Ending (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - proceed_to_throne 
 proceed_to_throne : After the player defeats Nashandra (or Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin, if his conditions are met) at the Throne of Want, a cutscene will play showing the player walking atop the golems, who create a bridge for the player to cross, and into a throne room. In this ending, the Bearer of the Curse will accept their part in the cycle of the world and take the throne. Doing so means that they will either sacrifice themselves to link the flame, or allow the flame to continue to fade and become the Dark Lord. Which the Bearer of the Curse chooses is known only to them.

title: Magerold of Lanafir
snippet: Magerold also displays a fascination with dragons, secretly being an adherent of the Dragon Remnants and seeking the location of the Dragon Shrine so he may find great treasures there. The Bearer of the Curse can bring him one such artifact, a mysterious stone egg, likely that of a dragon. Upon being given the fine specimen, he will allow the adventurer into his covenant.

title: Force (Dark Souls II)

Force (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - spell - general_information 
 general_information : Functions precisely how its *Dark Souls* variant works. Unleashes a force of energy around its caster, knocking back all enemies who are susceptible to such. It will deal no direct damage, however does have potential to indirectly cause fall damage to those caught in the blast. Primarily used to push enemies and invaders off cliffs.
